excerpt: Maggie Lenhart wrote that she manages the Del Taco relationship on the Worldpay side and is working through Del Taco’s contract renewal. Bryan Bailey mentioned that someone from Genius had a productive conversation with Daniel Meers at Genius World. Maggie asked to learn more about the discussion and requested an introduction to the individual who spoke with Daniel, hoping it could strengthen the broader Global Payments relationship and support future opportunities. Tracy Gallimore replied that she spoke briefly with Daniel before he departed, that he sounded like he had a good event and wants to know more about what a partnership looks like, and recommended scheduling a team call to review and strategize on next steps. Tracy also noted Todd Vahlsing was hired to partner with the Worldpay team on cross-sell opportunities.

excerpt: Dan reported that he worked with Del Taco during the former Jack in the Box ownership period and had strong rapport with Rob Stevens. Del Taco later explored a stopgap digital-menu-board concept that would retain static boards and place a roughly 32-inch screen in the center. The team held technical calls and considered Samsung and other options, but the desired system-on-chip approach did not align cleanly with the solution at the time and the effort went quiet around the divestiture. Dan described Del Taco's historical menu architecture as highly legacy and difficult to unwind, likely involving NCR; he recalled StrataCash getting an integration running quickly after Genius struggled with interim approaches. He said Qu won the broader Jack in the Box RFP, but does not believe Del Taco completed adoption. Rob Stevens and Dana King appear to have remained with Jack in the Box, so they may no longer provide direct access to Del Taco. Dan said Nick has an established relationship with Yadav and asked Nick to contact Todd with a Yadav overview and potential introduction. Todd noted that Worldpay recently renewed Del Taco and that Maggie is part of the cross-sell access strategy.
extracted_claims: Del Taco previously evaluated Genius for digital menu boards during the Jack in the Box ownership period.
The most recent historical DMB concept was a stopgap design using static menu boards with an approximately 32-inch screen in the center.
The desired system-on-chip configuration did not align cleanly with the Genius solution at the time, and the initiative went quiet around the Del Taco divestiture.
Rob Stevens was Dan's primary Del Taco advocate but now appears to remain with Jack in the Box, so his current relevance to Del Taco requires validation.
Del Taco's historical menu architecture was described as legacy and difficult to integrate, likely involving NCR; this is recollection and requires current-state validation.
Qu won the prior Jack in the Box RFP, but Dan does not believe Del Taco completed adoption; current Del Taco POS status remains unverified.
Nick has an established relationship with Yadav and agreed to contact Todd with a Yadav overview and possible introduction.
Worldpay recently renewed Del Taco, and Maggie is part of Todd's intended cross-sell access path.
limitations: Most account-history claims are retrospective recollections from the former Jack in the Box ownership period. Current vendor deployments, Rob Stevens' present influence, and Del Taco adoption of Qu or NCR require direct validation. The original base-model transcript was unusable; this evidence was extracted from a higher-accuracy retranscription of the same audio.

excerpt: Nick Hulayew reported that Yadav owns Denny's and Taco Cabana and that Dean, whom Nick described as Yadav's CTO, is a strong Genius advocate and customer advisory board member. Dean introduced Nick to Daniel Mears, whom Nick described as an IT director somewhere in the Del Taco IT organization. Nick invited Daniel to Genius World and met him there. Nick said Del Taco is looking across the whole technology stack in a comprehensive review, including payments, digital menu boards, POS hardware, and POS software. Nick agreed to text Daniel to continue the conversation and introduce Todd. Nick also reported that Anil Yadav is a silent investor in Qu and believes that relationship influenced the prior Jack in the Box decision; this is Nick's belief and requires validation. Nick said capital constraints may favor Genius because existing NCR hardware may be repurposed, avoiding the new hardware purchase he associates with Qu. He cited the Pollo Tropical NCR CX-5 retrofit from Windows to Android running Genius as a relevant proof point and offered to join calls and support the handoff.

Dean introduced Nick Hulayew to Daniel Mears, whom Nick described as an IT director within the Del Taco technology organization.
Nick Hulayew invited Daniel Mears to Genius World and met him there.

Nick Hulayew believes Anil Yadav is a silent investor in Qu and that the relationship influenced the prior Jack in the Box decision; this is reported belief and requires validation.

Nick Hulayew cited Pollo Tropical's conversion of NCR CX-5 devices from Windows to Android running Genius as a relevant retrofit proof point.

limitations: The recording contains substantial transcription noise. The core Del Taco discussion is intelligible, but Dean's surname and exact title, Daniel Mears' exact title and authority, Del Taco's review stage, capital availability, and the reported Anil Yadav–Qu investment relationship all require direct validation. The Qu investment statement is Nick Hulayew's belief, not a confirmed fact.
